summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low and inconsistent, with only 9 sessions logged across all disciplines and significant gaps between workouts. Sleep quality is a major concern, with multiple nights under 5 hours and body battery readings frequently in the 20-40 range, suggesting chronic under-recovery. The one high-intensity run on July 18th at HR 179 bpm stands out as a significant red flag given the poor recovery context surrounding it.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep immediately — multiple nights of 3-4 hours are severely limiting adaptation and injury resilience; target 7-8 hours consistently before attempting any quality sessions in the upcoming plan.

The July 30th plan stacks a 60-min strength session AND a 90-min cycling session on a day where body battery is 2-22 and sleep data is missing — reduce this to one session only (the cycling Z2 ride at lower end of power range) to avoid digging a deeper recovery hole.

Running pace for the marathon sub-4h goal (5:45/km target) is not being developed — current long runs at 6:15-6:45/km are appropriate base building, but ensure at least one run per week touches 6:00-6:15/km as aerobic capacity improves to close the gap to race pace.

Swimming sessions are very short and infrequent (longest was 52 min / 2km open water); the pool sessions starting July 31st are critical — commit to hitting the 2km+ target every session to build toward the Ironman 3.8km swim.

Avoid stacking high-load sessions (e.g. Wk7 cycling threshold intervals on Tuesday followed by strength + running on Thursday) when body battery trends remain low; use Wednesday rest days actively for breathwork and sleep extension rather than treating them as optional.
